fixes.explanation: Nope, friend, Paul never promises that. He says God comforts us "…in all our troubles…" (2 Corinthians 1:4), which means we're in the troubles when the comfort shows up. The reason Paul gives is that we can then "…comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God." (2 Corinthians 1:4). The comfort is for the middle of the mess, and then we pass it along.

Strength is a good word, friend, but it's not the one Paul uses here. He says, "…so also through Christ our comfort overflows." (2 Corinthians 1:5). Comfort is the thing that overflows right alongside the sufferings of Christ. I think Paul sure does love that word in these opening verses.

The Galatian churches are a fair guess, since Paul wrote to them in another letter (Galatians 1:1–2). But this letter is addressed to "…the church of God in Corinth…" (2 Corinthians 1:1). So the "your" in "your comfort" means the Corinthians. Same Paul, different mailbox.

That's it, baker! Paul says, "…our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort." (2 Corinthians 1:7). The Corinthians share in the sufferings now, and Paul says they will share in the comfort. So his hope for them stands on solid ground.

That's right, baker. Paul says, "We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure…" (2 Corinthians 1:8). That's not "a rough week." He's telling the Corinthians it was more than they could carry.

Paul doesn't say that, friend. The text says the burden was "…far beyond our ability to endure…" (2 Corinthians 1:8). Nothing in these verses says they quit or even slowed down. Paul says how heavy it was, and that "…we despaired even of life." (2 Corinthians 1:8).

Leaders are a fair guess, but Paul doesn't say it. The verse reads, "…in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead." (2 Corinthians 1:9). The blank is ourselves. The trust goes to God instead.

False is right, baker! Paul says, "He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us." (2 Corinthians 1:10). Then he keeps going: "In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us…" After that rescue, Paul's hope is still on God to deliver again.

Letters would be nice, friend, and Paul is writing one right now. But the word in this verse is prayers: "…as you help us by your prayers." (2 Corinthians 1:11). Paul says their prayers are how they help him. And then he says "many will give thanks on our behalf" for the favor shown in answer to those prayers.
